PROP
40
IMPOSES ONE-TIME TAX ON CERTAIN TAXPAYERS. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT AND STATUTE.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Imposes 5% tax on certain taxpayers with assets over $1 billion; revenue primarily for health care. Exempts revenues from constitutional requirements for school funding and spending limit. Fiscal Impact: Temporary revenue increase of tens of billions of dollars spread over several years from wealth tax on billionaires. Possible ongoing decrease of less than $1 billion per year in income tax revenue from billionaires. Supporters: US Senator Bernie Sanders; SEIU United Healthcare Workers West Opponents: California Primary Care Association; California School Boards Association; California Taxpayers Association
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: The state would collect a one-time tax from billionaires equal to 5 percent of their wealth.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: The state would not collect a one-time tax from billionaires equal to 5 percent of their wealth.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
Vote YES on 40 to tax billionaires. Trump slashed healthcare funding to pay for billionaire tax breaks, eliminating coverage for over a million Californians and doubling health insurance premiums for millions more. It’s time to make billionaires pay their fair share and stop sticking the middle class with the bill.
CON
Prop. 40 is a flawed, one-time tax scheme that hurts our economy, damages our state budget, and contains a loophole exposing all Californians to taxes we can’t afford—but does nothing to lower healthcare costs. No safeguards, no accountability. Join California Teachers Association, California Medical Association, California Children’s Hospital Association, California Professional Firefighters, State Building and Construction Trades Council of California, Democrats and Republicans: NO on 40.

# Proposition 40: One-Time Wealth Tax
## Proposition 40: Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers. Initiative Constitutional Amendment and Statute.
### Additional Titles
One-Time Wealth Tax for State-Funded Health Care Programs Initiative
### Summary
Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5 percent tax on the net worth of billionaires who were California residents on January 1, 2026.
The tax would be collected beginning in 2027, with an option to pay over five years at a higher total cost.
Real estate, pensions, and retirement accounts generally would not be included when calculating taxable wealth.
The state would have some discretion on how and when to spend the money from the tax, as long as 90 percent of the revenue is used to support public health care services, with the remaining funds available for education, food assistance, and costs associated with administering the tax.
The money would be exempt from certain existing state constitutional spending requirements.
Proposition 40 could also be prevented from taking effect if Proposition 41 or 42 receives more votes and courts determine that the measures conflict.
...
### What your vote means
YES: A “yes” vote supports a one-time 5% tax on taxable wealth above $1 billion, with the revenue primarily funding health care, as well as food assistance and public education.
No: A “no” vote opposes creating this one-time wealth tax.
### Official Voter Information
- California Secretary of State, Official Voter Information, Quic

# Proposition 40

## Analysis of Measure
### Proposal
***Establishes One-Time Wealth Tax on Billionaires.*** Under Proposition 40, billionaires who were residents of California on January 1, 2026 would have to pay a one-time state tax equal to 5 percent of their net worth.
The tax would be due in 2027.
Taxpayers would have the option to spread the payments over five years but would have to pay more to do so.
Real estate, pensions, and retirement accounts generally would be excluded from the tax.
***Most of the Money Must Be Spent on Health Care.*** The state would decide how and when to spend the money from the wealth tax, but it would have to be spent on certain types of services.
Ninety percent of the money would have to be spent on health care services for the public.
The rest would have to be spent on education, food assistance, and administration of the wealth tax.
Existing rules in the State Constitution that limit spending and require the state to spend a certain amount on schools and community colleges would not apply to this money.
...

A **YES** vote on this measure means: The state would collect a one-time tax from billionaires equal to 5 percent of their wealth.

# Proposition 40
Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers.
Initiative Constitutional Amendment and Statute.
## Analysis of Measure
### Proposal
***Establishes One-Time Wealth Tax on Billionaires.*** Under Proposition 40, billionaires who were residents of California on January 1, 2026 would have to pay a one-time state tax equal to 5 percent of their net worth.
The tax would be due in 2027.
Taxpayers would have the option to spread the payments over five years but would have to pay more to do so.
Real estate, pensions, and retirement accounts generally would be excluded from the tax.
***Most of the Money Must Be Spent on Health Care.*** The state would decide how and when to spend the money from the wealth tax, but it would have to be spent on certain types of services.
Ninety percent of the money would have to be spent on health care services for the public.
The rest would have to be spent on education, food assistance, and administration of the wealth tax.
Existing rules in the State Constitution that limit spending and require the state to spend a certain amount on schools and community colleges would not apply to this money.

|Proposition 40|Require the state's billionaires would pay a one-time 5% wealth tax, including businesses, securities, shares of capital stock and bonds, art, collectibles, and intellectual property.
Real property and some pensions and retirement accounts would be exempt.
90% of the revenue generated would fund Medi-Cal and other health care programs, and 10% on food assistance or education-related programs.
It also mandates that the revenue would supplement, not replace, the existing funding for these programs.^[28]^| | | | |Citizen-initiated constitutional amendment|

PROP
40
IMPOSES ONE-TIME TAX ON CERTAIN TAXPAYERS. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT AND STATUTE.
SUMMARY
Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures
Imposes 5% tax on certain taxpayers with assets over $1 billion; revenue primarily for health care. Exempts revenues from constitutional requirements for school funding and spending limit. Fiscal Impact: Temporary revenue increase of tens of billions of dollars spread over several years from wealth tax on billionaires. Possible ongoing decrease of less than $1 billion per year in income tax revenue from billionaires. Supporters: US Senator Bernie Sanders; SEIU United Healthcare Workers West Opponents: California Primary Care Association; California School Boards Association; California Taxpayers Association
WHAT YOUR VOTE MEANS
YES
A YES vote on this measure means: The state would collect a one-time tax from billionaires equal to 5 percent of their wealth.
NO
A NO vote on this measure means: The state would not collect a one-time tax from billionaires equal to 5 percent of their wealth.
ARGUMENTS
PRO
Vote YES on 40 to tax billionaires. Trump slashed healthcare funding to pay for billionaire tax breaks, eliminating coverage for over a million Californians and doubling health insurance premiums for millions more. It’s time to make billionaires pay their fair share and stop sticking the middle class with the bill.
CON
Prop. 40 is a flawed, one-time tax scheme that hurts our economy, damages our state budget, and contains a loophole exposing all Californians to taxes we can’t afford—but does nothing to lower healthcare costs. No safeguards, no accountability. Join California Teachers Association, California Medical Association, California Children’s Hospital Association, California Professional Firefighters, State Building and Construction Trades Council of California, Democrats and Republicans: NO on 40.

### Additional Titles

### Summary
Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5 percent tax on the net worth of billionaires who were California residents on January 1, 2026.
The tax would be collected beginning in 2027, with an option to pay over five years at a higher total cost.
Real estate, pensions, and retirement accounts generally would not be included when calculating taxable wealth.
The state would have some discretion on how and when to spend the money from the tax, as long as 90 percent of the revenue is used to support public health care services, with the remaining funds available for education, food assistance, and costs associated with administering the tax.
The money would be exempt from certain existing state constitutional spending requirements.
Proposition 40 could also be prevented from taking effect if Proposition 41 or 42 receives more votes and courts determine that the measures conflict.
